name: GA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals: a D+25 lean plus a favorable environment point strongly to Democrats
McBath's overwhelming fundraising edge, roughly $1.15 million raised versus about $10,000 for Martin
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 96 percent

model.rationale: A D+25 district, a favorable environment, and an incumbency edge all favor McBath, and her fundraising advantage over Martin is roughly one hundred to one. Markets price her win odds near 96 percent, and with no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow the margin, though it would take a historic change to alter the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 6th District leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Lucy McBath returns as the clear favorite after renomination. The fundamentals point strongly her way: a district lean of roughly 25 points Democratic, a favorable political environment, and the usual incumbency edge. Republican Kevin Martin has run a minimal campaign, reporting about ten thousand dollars raised and one hundred dollars on hand, while McBath has raised over one million and holds more than six hundred thousand in reserve. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Those signals all point the same direction, toward a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-to-high twenties. The main uncertainty is the absence of direct polling, which keeps confidence from being fully firm.
